key_insight: AutoMem treats memory management as a learnable skill for LLM agents, jointly optimizing the memory system design and the agent’s ability to use memory well.
engineering_relevance: For long-horizon agent systems, improving memory alone can yield large performance gains without changing core task behavior, making it a high-leverage optimization target.
method: A strong LLM reviews full agent trajectories and iteratively redesigns memory structure: prompts, file schemas, and action vocabulary.
Memory operations are promoted to first-class actions so the agent decides when to encode, retrieve, and organize information.
Good memory decisions from many episodes are distilled into training signals to improve the agent’s memory proficiency.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on three procedurally generated long-horizon games—Crafter, MiniHack, and NetHack—where memory optimization alone improved performance by about 2x to 4x and made a 32B open-weight model competitive with frontier systems.
watch_item: The approach depends on large-scale trajectory review and long episodes, so its effectiveness may hinge on strong evaluators and careful handling of rare but impactful memory mistakes.
paper_title: AutoMem: Automated Learning of Memory as a Cognitive Skill
